newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money drops back on good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money drops back on good liquidity.

text.p: Croatian interbank call money rates dropped back to 10.5 percent on Wednesday from Tuesday's 11 percent thanks to improved liquidity, dealers said.
"The day started with a good supply of kuna, the morning trade ending with an extra 25 million kuna or so on the supply side," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She added that better liquidity was spurred by the central bank decision to lower mandatory reserve requirement for banks by one percentage point this month.
This in turn prompted banks to repay old borrowings which were due later, Blagaic added.
The government's payment in kuna for part of its liabilities on the frozen foreign exchange debt also helped.
Total morning dealings were put at 35.8 million kuna, most of which were call money deals at 10.5 percent. The exception was a single loan to a savings bank granted at 11 percent.
Term rates ranged between a steady 13 percent for two-week funds and 17 percent for one-month and two-month loans.
There was no overnight trade on Tuesday with banks' accounts totalling 608.5 million kuna without any shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
